claim: Wilms Tumor 1 (WT1) is a zinc finger transcription factor that regulates key developmental stages of several mesodermal tissues including the kidneys, gonads and coronary vasculature.
source: Wilms tumour 1 (WT1) is a zinc finger transcription factor that regulates key developmental stages of several mesodermal tissues including the kidneys, gonads and coronary vasculature (Hastie, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hastie, 2017.

claim: In the developing kidney, WT1 is required for the maintenance of mesenchymal nephron progenitors.
source: In the developing kidney, WT1 is required for the maintenance of mesenchymal nephron progenitors (Kreidberg et al., 1993; Motamedi et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Kreidberg et al., 1993 and Motamedi et al., 2014.

claim: WT1 is required for differentiation of mesenchymal nephron progenitors into the epithelial components of the nephron.
source: In the developing kidney, WT1 is required for the maintenance of mesenchymal nephron progenitors (Kreidberg et al., 1993; Motamedi et al., 2014) as well as differentiation of these progenitors into the epithelial components of the nephron (Essafi et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Essafi et al., 2011.

claim: In the developing heart, WT1 is expressed in the epicardium.
source: In contrast, in the developing heart, WT1 is expressed in the epicardium (mesothelial lining) and required for the production, via an epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT), of coronary vascular progenitors (EPDCs) that migrate into the myocardium (Martínez-Estrada et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Martínez-Estrada et al., 2010.

claim: WT1 is required for the production of coronary vascular progenitors via an epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) that migrate into the myocardium.
source: In contrast, in the developing heart, WT1 is expressed in the epicardium (mesothelial lining) and required for the production, via an epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT), of coronary vascular progenitors (EPDCs) that migrate into the myocardium (Martínez-Estrada et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Martínez-Estrada et al., 2010.

claim: WT1-expressing mesothelium is the source of mesenchymal progenitors for stellate cells within the liver.
source: Similarly, WT1-expressing mesothelium is the source of mesenchymal progenitors for specialised cell types within several other developing organs. These include stellate cells within the liver (Asahina et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Asahina et al., 2011.

claim: WT1-expressing mesothelium is the source of mesenchymal progenitors for interstitial cells of Cajal in the intestine.
source: These include stellate cells within the liver (Asahina et al., 2011), interstitial cells of Cajal in the intestine (Carmona et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Carmona et al., 2013.

claim: WT1-expressing mesothelium is the source of mesenchymal progenitors for adipocytes within visceral fat depots.
source: These include stellate cells within the liver (Asahina et al., 2011), interstitial cells of Cajal in the intestine (Carmona et al., 2013) and adipocytes within visceral fat depots (Chau et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chau et al., 2014.

claim: WT1 expression is down-regulated in the epicardium postnatally but reactivated in response to tissue damage in both mice and zebrafish.
source: WT1 expression is down-regulated in the epicardium postnatally but reactivated in response to tissue damage in both mice (Smart et al., 2011) and zebrafish (Schnabel et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Smart et al., 2011 and Schnabel et al., 2011.

claim: Activation of WT1 in response to damage is associated with new rounds of epicardial EMT, leading to the production of coronary vascular progenitors in both mice and zebrafish.
source: In both organisms, this activation of WT1 in response to damage is associated with new rounds of epicardial EMT, leading to the production of coronary vascular progenitors (Schnabel et al., 2011; Smart et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schnabel et al., 2011 and Smart et al., 2011.

claim: The notochord is a transient embryonic structure that provides axial support and signalling information.
source: The notochord is a transient embryonic structure that provides axial support and signalling information (Stemple, 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stemple, 2005.

claim: The notochord comprises inner vacuolated cells that provide rigid support to the embryo.
source: The notochord comprises two cell populations, the inner vacuolated cells that provide rigid support to the embryo, and the outer sheath cells
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: The notochord comprises outer sheath cells, a single cell epithelial layer that surrounds the vacuolated cells and secretes components of the extracellular matrix to provide turgor pressure to the vacuolated cells.
source: The notochord comprises two cell populations, the inner vacuolated cells that provide rigid support to the embryo, and the outer sheath cells, a single cell epithelial layer that surrounds the vacuolated cells and secretes components of the extracellular matrix to provide turgor pressure to the vacuolated cells (Apschner et al., 2011; Ellis et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Apschner et al., 2011 and Ellis et al., 2013.

claim: In zebrafish, a row of metameric mineralized rings, known as chordacentra, forms around the notochord in an anterior to posterior fashion and constitutes the first signs of the definitive vertebral column.
source: In zebrafish, a row of metameric mineralized rings, known as chordacentra, forms around the notochord in an anterior to posterior fashion and constitutes the first signs of the definitive vertebral column.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: The chordacentra delineate the future sites where mature vertebra will form and ossify as the larva grows.
source: The chordacentra delineate the future sites where mature vertebra will form and ossify as the larva grows, while the notochord cells develop into the nucleus pulposus of the adult intervertebral disc
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text.

claim: Notochord cells develop into the nucleus pulposus of the adult intervertebral disc, a soft gel-like tissue that provides cushioning and flexibility for the spine.
source: while the notochord cells develop into the nucleus pulposus of the adult intervertebral disc, a soft gel-like tissue that provides cushioning and flexibility for the spine (Parsons, 1977).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Parsons, 1977.

claim: Degeneration of the intervertebral disc leads to extensive back pain, one of the top global causes of years lived with disability.
source: Degeneration of the intervertebral disc leads to extensive back pain, one of the top global causes of years lived with disability (Lawson and Harfe, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lawson and Harfe, 2015.

claim: Tail fin amputations including partial removal of the notochord triggered a change of cellularity in the notochord, coupled with the specific, de novo upregulation of GFP in a Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgenic line.
source: Surprisingly, we discovered that tail fin amputations including partial removal of the notochord triggered a change of cellularity in the notochord, coupled with the specific, de novo upregulation of GFP in a Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgenic line.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and supported by experimental observations.

claim: Tail fin amputation response was specific to wt1b because no expression of GFP was observed in the notochord of Tg(wt1a:gfp) tail fin amputated larvae.
source: This response was specific to wt1b because we did not observe expression of GFP in the notochord of Tg(wt1a:gfp) tail fin amputated larvae (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b–f.

claim: Needle induced wounds triggered a wt1b:gfp response that was specifically localised to the site of the wound.
source: Needle induced wounds triggered a similar, albeit stronger wt1b:gfp response compared to the tail fin amputations, that was specifically localised to the site of the wound (Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Time course imaging showed a progressive expansion of the damaged area over 72 hr, with an increasing expression of GFP signal, concomitant with a change of cellularity in the notochord.
source: Time course imaging showed a progressive expansion of the damaged area over 72 hr, with an increasing expression of GFP signal, concomitant with a change of cellularity in the notochord (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Histological staining of the damaged area revealed the presence of a subpopulation of cells at the site of injury, which contrasted morphologically with the uniform, vacuolated inner cells of the notochord.
source: Histological staining of the damaged area revealed the presence of a subpopulation of cells at the site of injury, which contrasted morphologically with the uniform, vacuolated inner cells of the notochord (Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Cells at the site of injury stained positively for GFP and for endogenous Wt1 protein by immunohistochemistry, validating the faithful expression of the transgene with endogenous wt1b expression in this response.
source: These cells stained positively for GFP and for endogenous Wt1 protein by immunohistochemistry, validating the faithful expression of the transgene with endogenous wt1b expression in this response (Figure 1e; Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Tg(wt1b:gfp) expression was not detected in the notochord outside the wound response by immunohistochemistry for GFP or for Wt1 protein.
source: Tg(wt1b:gfp) expression was not detected in the notochord outside the wound response by immunohistochemistry for GFP or for Wt1 protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Following notochord injury, an unanticipated expression of wt1b marks a subpopulation of cells that emerges in the notochord and is associated with the wound.
source: Thus, following notochord injury, an unanticipated expression of wt1b marks a subpopulation of cells that emerges in the notochord and is associated with the wound.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Live confocal and multiphoton imaging revealed wt1b:gfp expression in the R2col2a1a:mCherry notochord sheath cells following needle induced notochord damage.
source: Live confocal and multiphoton imaging revealed wt1b:gfp expression in the R2col2a1a:mCherry notochord sheath cells following needle induced notochord damage (Figure 2b–d; Video 1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1c)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b–d, Video 1, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: wt1b:gfp co-expression with R2col2a1a:mCherry was visible by 24 hpi in a ring surrounding the notochord vacuolated cells.
source: wt1b:gfp co-expression with R2col2a1a:mCherry was visible by 24 hpi in a ring surrounding the notochord vacuolated cells
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and supported by experimental observations.

claim: By 72 hpi the wt1b:gfp subpopulation of sheath cells had migrated into central aspects of the notochord to fill the wound and produce a visible stopper-like seal that was contiguous with the notochord sheath cells.
source: by 72 hpi the wt1b:gfp subpopulation of sheath cells had migrated into central aspects of the notochord to fill the wound and produce a visible stopper-like seal that was contiguous with the notochord sheath cells, and filled the gap in the notochord caused by the wound (Figures 1e and 2d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1e and 2d.

claim: Wounded fish had significantly increased numbers of cells that co-expressed wt1b:gfp and col2a1a:mCherry (GFP+mCherry+) compared to non-injured larvae.
source: Both injured and non-injured larvae contained cells that expressed either GFP+ only (presumably wt1b:gfp cells of the pronephric duct that were included in the dissected tissue) or mCherry+ alone, but the wounded fish had significantly increased numbers of cells that co-expressed wt1b:gfp and col2a1a:mCherry (GFP+mCherry+) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e.

claim: The notochord wound triggers a unique wt1b+ subpopulation to emerge in the notochord sheath cells.
source: Our evidence indicates that the notochord wound triggers a unique wt1b+ subpopulation to emerge in the notochord sheath cells.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The wt1b+ sheath cell subpopulation migrates into the wound and generates a stopper-like structure, possibly to prevent further loss of notochord turgor pressure and maintain notochord integrity.
source: This wt1b+ sheath cell subpopulation migrates into the wound and generates a stopper-like structure, possibly to prevent further loss of notochord turgor pressure and maintain notochord integrity.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented, with speculation about the function.

claim: Nystatin treatment lead to an increase in cellularity of the vacuolated notochord, similar to the phenotype seen in the notochord of caveolin mutants.
source: Nystatin treatment lead to an increase in cellularity of the vacuolated notochord, similar to the phenotype seen in the notochord of caveolin mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Expression of wt1b in the sheath does not require a physical breach of the sheath.
source: Thus, expression of wt1b in the sheath does not require a physical breach of the sheath, and wt1b expression may be applicable to a wider range of tissue stress and damage situations.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the nystatin treatment experiment.

claim: Microarray analysis revealed a highly significant 131-fold increase in expression of matrix gla protein (mgp) in injured larvae compared to uninjured controls.
source: Microarray analysis revealed a highly significant 131-fold increase in expression of matrix gla protein (mgp), a gene that is known to express in chondrocytic zebrafish tissues (Gavaia et al., 2006) and to be involved in the inhibition of hydroxyapatite production during ectopic bone formation (Schurgers et al., 2013; Sweatt et al., 2003; Zebboudj et al., 2002) (Figure 3c,d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3c,d.

claim: Matrix gla protein (mgp) is known to express in chondrocytic zebrafish tissues.
source: Microarray analysis revealed a highly significant 131-fold increase in expression of matrix gla protein (mgp), a gene that is known to express in chondrocytic zebrafish tissues (Gavaia et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gavaia et al., 2006.

claim: Matrix gla protein (mgp) is involved in the inhibition of hydroxyapatite production during ectopic bone formation.
source: a gene that is known to express in chondrocytic zebrafish tissues (Gavaia et al., 2006) and to be involved in the inhibition of hydroxyapatite production during ectopic bone formation (Schurgers et al., 2013; Sweatt et al., 2003; Zebboudj et al., 2002)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Schurgers et al., 2013; Sweatt et al., 2003; Zebboudj et al., 2002.

claim: Other genes upregulated in injured tissue included mesenchymal and cell adhesion markers, such as fn1b, coagulation factors, such as f13a1b, and immune response genes, such as zgc:92041 and complement c6.
source: Other genes included mesenchymal and cell adhesion markers, such as fn1b, coagulation factors, such as f13a1b, and immune response genes, such as zgc:92041 and complement c6 (Figure 3d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Analysis of the top 100 significant genes found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis.
source: To examine the expression of other chondrogenic genes, we analyzed the top 100 significant genes and found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from microarray analysis.

claim: Analysis of the top 100 significant genes found an increase in expression of five collagen genes associated with chondrogenic tissues (col2a1a, col2a1b, col11a2, col9a1 and col9a2).
source: we analyzed the top 100 significant genes and found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis, five collagen genes associated with chondrogenic tissues (col2a1a, col2a1b, col11a2, col9a1 and col9a2)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from microarray analysis.

claim: Analysis of the top 100 significant genes found an increase in expression of the cartilage-specific extracellular structural protein Aggrecan.
source: we analyzed the top 100 significant genes and found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis, five collagen genes associated with chondrogenic tissues (col2a1a, col2a1b, col11a2, col9a1 and col9a2), the cartilage-specific extracellular structural protein Aggrecan
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from microarray analysis.

claim: Analysis of the top 100 significant genes found an increase in expression of a microRNA regulator of chondrogenesis microRNA140.
source: we analyzed the top 100 significant genes and found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis, five collagen genes associated with chondrogenic tissues (col2a1a, col2a1b, col11a2, col9a1 and col9a2), the cartilage-specific extracellular structural protein Aggrecan, a microRNA regulator of chondrogenesis microRNA140
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from microarray analysis.

claim: Analysis of the top 100 significant genes found an increase in expression of the matrix-cell anchor protein chondroadherin (chad).
source: we analyzed the top 100 significant genes and found an increase in expression of sox9b, the master regulator of chondrogenesis, five collagen genes associated with chondrogenic tissues (col2a1a, col2a1b, col11a2, col9a1 and col9a2), the cartilage-specific extracellular structural protein Aggrecan, a microRNA regulator of chondrogenesis microRNA140 and the matrix-cell anchor protein chondroadherin (chad) (Figure 3e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: qRT-PCR validation found mgp to be highly upregulated in the injured tissue compared with the uninjured tissue.
source: To validate these findings at the molecular level, we isolated sections of damaged and undamaged tissue, and performed qRT-PCR for matrix gla protein (mgp) and sox9b. We chose these two genes because mgp was highly expressed in the microarray analysis and important for bone organization, and because Sox9 is a master cartilage transcription factor. We found mgp and sox9b to be highly upregulated in the injured tissue compared with the uninjured tissue (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f,g.

claim: qRT-PCR validation found sox9b to be highly upregulated in the injured tissue compared with the uninjured tissue.
source: We found mgp and sox9b to be highly upregulated in the injured tissue compared with the uninjured tissue (Figure 3f,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3f,g.

claim: Notochord wounding leads to the formation of a wt1b-positive sheath subpopulation that is characterised by an unexpected increase in genes associated with cartilage.
source: Our results reveal that notochord wounding leads to the formation of a wt1b-positive sheath subpopulation that is characterised by an unexpected increase in genes associated with cartilage.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Unbiased Single cell consensus clustering (SC3) of the whole transcriptomes revealed that the GFP+ cells, mCherry+ cells and GFP+mCherry+ cells clustered into three distinct subpopulations.
source: Unbiased Single cell consensus clustering (SC3) of the whole transcriptomes revealed that the GFP+ cells, mCherry+ cells and GFP+mCherry+ cells clustered into three distinct subpopulations (SC3 cluster 1: GFP+, 2: GFP+mCherry+ and 3: mCherry+) (Figure 4a–c) (Kiselev et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a–c.

claim: Expression of wt1b was detected in SC3 clusters 1 and 2.
source: Expression of wt1b was detected in SC3 clusters 1 and 2, and col2a1a was expressed in SC3 clusters 2 and 3 (Figure 4b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: col2a1a was expressed in SC3 clusters 2 and 3.
source: Expression of wt1b was detected in SC3 clusters 1 and 2, and col2a1a was expressed in SC3 clusters 2 and 3 (Figure 4b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: wt1a transcripts were not detected in any of the SC3 clusters.
source: wt1a transcripts were not detected in any of the SC3 clusters.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and supported by experimental observations.

claim: Detection of wt1b transcripts in GFP+mCherry+ cells prove endogenous wt1b expression in the notochord damage response.
source: Together with the Wt1b antibody immunohistochemistry (Figure 1e, Figure 1—figure supplement 2), detection of wt1b transcripts in GFP+mCherry+ cells prove endogenous wt1b expression in the notochord damage response.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Differential marker gene expression in GFP+mCherry+ cells included the mgp, fn1b and f13a1b genes that were highly upregulated in the wounded tissue.
source: Notably, differential marker gene expression in GFP+mCherry+ cells included the mgp, fn1b and f13a1b genes (Figure 4c) that were highly upregulated in the wounded tissue (Figure 3d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4c and Figure 3d.

claim: qRT-PCR validation found expression of mgp was selectively enriched in GFP+mCherry+ double positive cells.
source: To validate our findings, we isolated injured notochord tissue from 3dpi and FACS sorted GFP+, mCherry+ and GFP+mCherry+ double positive cells, and performed qRT-PCR on sorted cell populations for mgp, a SC3 cluster 2 cell marker gene. Expression of mgp was selectively enriched in GFP+mCherry+ double positive cells (Figure 4d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4d.

claim: Expression of genes in signaling pathways, such as the TGF-ß pathway were reduced in GFP+mCherry+ cells compared with mCherry+ cells.
source: Expression of genes in signaling pathways, such as the TGF-ß pathway were reduced, while vacuolar and lysosomal pathway components were highly enriched in the GFP+mCherry+ cells comparing gene sets from multiple databases.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from functional analysis.

claim: Vacuolar and lysosomal pathway components were highly enriched in the GFP+mCherry+ cells compared with mCherry+ cells.
source: Expression of genes in signaling pathways, such as the TGF-ß pathway were reduced, while vacuolar and lysosomal pathway components were highly enriched in the GFP+mCherry+ cells comparing gene sets from multiple databases.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from functional analysis.

claim: Confocal imaging analysis of the wound site at 7 dpi observed some GFP+mCherry+ cells with large inclusions (presumably vacuoles), in the cytoplasm.
source: To explore the possibility of lysosome activity in more detail, we performed confocal imaging analysis of the wound site at 7 dpi and observed some GFP+mCherry+ cells with large inclusions (presumably vacuoles), in the cytoplasm (Figure 4f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4f.

claim: Some GFP+mCherry+ cells may become vacuolated to replace those lost upon injury.
source: This suggests that some GFP+mCherry+ cells may become vacuolated to replace those lost upon injury.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Cartilage genes were significantly enriched in the cell cluster 2 (GFP+mCherry+ cells) compared with cell cluster 3 (mCherry+ cells).
source: Cartilage genes were significantly enriched in the cell cluster 2 (GFP+mCherry+ cells) compared with cell cluster 3 (mCherry+ cells), suggesting that it is specifically the wt1b-expressing sheath cells that express genes involved in cartilage formation (Figure 4g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: It is specifically the wt1b-expressing sheath cells that express genes involved in cartilage formation.
source: Cartilage genes were significantly enriched in the cell cluster 2 (GFP+mCherry+ cells) compared with cell cluster 3 (mCherry+ cells), suggesting that it is specifically the wt1b-expressing sheath cells that express genes involved in cartilage formation (Figure 4g).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the gene set enrichment analysis.

claim: A set of WT1 regulated genes were specifically repressed in the GFP+mCherry+ cells.
source: Unexpectedly, we discovered a set of WT1 regulated genes that were specifically repressed in the GFP+mCherry+ cells (Figure 4h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4h.

claim: Wt1b may function as a repressor in the notochord damage response.
source: WT1 can function with co-factors to repress or activate gene expression, and this new signature suggests that Wt1b may function as a repressor in the notochord damage response.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: p53 was most differentially expressed in GFP+mCherry+ cells compared with mCherry+ cells among all WT1 co-transcription factors.
source: Next, we performed gene expression analysis for all WT1 co-transcription factors described in (Toska and Roberts, 2014), and found p53 to be most differentially expressed in GFP+mCherry+ cells compared with mCherry+ cells (Figure 4i,j).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4i,j.

claim: p53 target genes are enriched overall in the GFP+mCherry+ cell populations.
source: GSEA analysis showed that p53 target genes are enriched overall in the GFP+mCherry+ cell populations (Figure 4k; Supplementary file 1b, 1e)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4k.

claim: There was a strong repression of genes that are regulated by both WT1 and p53 in GFP+mCherry+ cells.
source: however, when we specifically analysed the gene expression for those genes that were present in both the WT1 and p53 target gene list (Supplementary file 1f), we found a strong repression of genes that are regulated by both WT1 and p53 (Figure 4l).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4l.

claim: An unexpected co-operation between Wt1b and p53 negatively regulates a select subset of genes in the wt1b-expressing sheath cell subpopulation during the wound response.
source: These data uncover an unexpected co-operation between Wt1b and p53 to negatively regulate a select subset of genes in the wt1b-expressing sheath cell subpopulation during the wound response.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Cartilage was clearly visible at the site of injury as soon as three dpi.
source: Cartilage was clearly visible at the site of injury as soon as three dpi (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Cartilage staining at the injury site was significantly stronger and distinct from the highly coordinated segmental cartilage staining that normally occurs during larval development in the region of the future intervertebral discs.
source: This staining was significantly stronger and distinct from the highly coordinated segmental cartilage staining that normally occurs during larval development in the region of the future intervertebral discs, which is clearly visible in both injured and non-injured controls by 14 dpi (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: In injured zebrafish larvae, the normally uniform mineralization pattern was interrupted around the site of damage, leading to delayed formation of the chordacentra at later stages.
source: Similarly, the alizarin red dye identified the anterior to posterior forming chordacentra rings during larval development. However, in injured zebrafish larvae, the normally uniform mineralization pattern was interrupted around the site of damage, leading to delayed formation of the chordacentra at later stages (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: By 18 dpi, the injured site began to express bone matrix, and was visibly flanked by cartilage expressing segments.
source: By 18 dpi, the injured site began to express bone matrix, and was visibly flanked by cartilage expressing segments (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: During norm-physiological development of the vertebral elements, cartilage and bone stains mark distinct regions of the notochord.
source: This is unusual because during norm-physiological development of the vertebral elements, cartilage and bone stains mark distinct regions of the notochord.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and represents established knowledge.

claim: The vertebrae that eventually formed at the injury site were often smaller in a given space interval and appeared supernumerary compared with uninjured age-matched controls.
source: To evaluate the outcome of the injury in the ossification process, wild-type larvae were injured and stained using live calcein dye at 21 and 38 dpi (Du et al., 2001). The vertebrae that eventually formed were often smaller in a given space interval and appeared supernumerary compared with uninjured age-matched controls (Figure 5c–e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c–e.

claim: Metameric expression of entpd5a in notochord sheath cells is an essential requirement for the patterned formation of chordacentra rings.
source: Recent evidence shows that metameric expression of entpd5a in notochord sheath cells is an essential requirement for the patterned formation of chordacentra rings (LL-F and SS-M, personal communication)
evidence: The claim is supported by personal communication cited in the manuscript.

claim: entpd5a expression serves as a readout for mineralizing activity.
source: with entpd5a expression serving as a readout for mineralizing activity (Huitema et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Huitema et al., 2012.

claim: wt1b and entpd5a expressing cell populations were closely associated at the wound site.
source: We crossed the Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgenic line to a Tg(entdp5a:pkRed) line and followed the wound response. wt1b and entpd5a expressing cell populations were closely associated at the wound site indicating that mineralizing entpd5a cells may directly contribute to wt1b+ associated chordacentra response (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a,b.

claim: Mineralizing entpd5a cells may directly contribute to wt1b+ associated chordacentra response.
source: wt1b and entpd5a expressing cell populations were closely associated at the wound site indicating that mineralizing entpd5a cells may directly contribute to wt1b+ associated chordacentra response (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Fish that had been wounded between the entpd5a-expression domains appeared to have normal vertebrae structures at 25 dpi.
source: We wounded the notochord in 5 dpf and 7dpf fish either in between two adjacent entpd5a-expression domains or aimed at the center of an entpd5a-expression domain. Fish that had been wounded between the entpd5a-expression domains appeared to have normal vertebrae structures at 25 dpi (n = 6/6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Damaging the entpd5a-expression domain led to a supernumerary vertebra at the wound site.
source: In contrast, damaging the entpd5a-expression domain led to a supernumerary vertebra at the wound site (n = 4/4; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Wounding alone is not sufficient to alter the vertebrae number.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that wounding alone is not sufficient to alter the vertebrae number, and that entpd5a expression domains likely play a role in vertebrae formation following injury.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: entpd5a expression domains likely play a role in vertebrae formation following injury.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that wounding alone is not sufficient to alter the vertebrae number, and that entpd5a expression domains likely play a role in vertebrae formation following injury.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data.

claim: The notochord wound assay at 3 dpf may disrupt an as of yet unknown precursor cell population.
source: These experiments raise the possibility that the notochord wound assay at 3 dpf disrupts an as of yet unknown precursor cell population.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Up-regulation of entpd5a at the damage site may be part of a patho-physiological wound repair response that disrupts and/or engages with a precursor cell population leading to altered vertebra(e) in the adult.
source: Up-regulation of entpd5a at the damage site may be part of a patho-physiological wound repair response that disrupts and/or engages with a precursor cell population (such as the metameric entpd5a expression) leading to altered vertebra(e) in the adult.
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgene expression was always associated with the site of vertebrae formation in the injured zebrafish that were raised to adulthood.
source: We noticed that the Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgene expression was always associated with the site of vertebrae formation in the injured zebrafish that were raised to adulthood.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the manuscript text and supported by experimental observations.

claim: GFP expression was sustained at the wound site, remaining in a small, cellular population at the site of damage, even as chordacentra developed and mineralized around the notochord over time.
source: GFP expression was sustained at the wound site, remaining in a small, cellular population at the site of damage, even as chordacentra developed and mineralized around the notochord over time (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgene maintained expression at the injury site up to 38 dpi.
source: Strikingly, the Tg(wt1b:gfp) transgene maintained expression at this site up to 38 dpi (Figure 7c,d,g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7c,d,g.

claim: wt1b:gfp expressing cells both mark a subpopulation of cells that are rapidly activated at the site of the wound and also that these cells persist until adulthood, possibly orchestrating local vertebrae formation with wound repair.
source: Taken together these results indicate that wt1b:gfp expressing cells both mark a subpopulation of cells that are rapidly activated at the site of the wound and also that these cells persist until adulthood, possibly orchestrating local vertebrae formation with wound repair.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Notochord sheath cells can sense and respond to different types of damage.
source: These studies highlight a previously unknown complex and heterogeneous nature of the sheath cell populations, and suggest that the notochord sheath can sense and respond to different types of damage.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Motion-dependent shear stress in caveolin mutants causes loss of vacuolated cells that are replaced by new vacuolated cells that arise from the sheath.
source: Motion-dependent shear stress in caveolin mutants causes loss of vacuolated cells that are replaced by new vacuolated cells that arise from the sheath (Garcia et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Garcia et al., 2017.

claim: Acute damage (i.e. needle injury) that encompasses sheath and vacuolated cell damage, leads to sheath cells forming a seal that marks the site of new cartilage and vertebra.
source: while acute damage (i.e. needle injury) that encompasses sheath and vacuolated cell damage, leads to sheath cells forming a seal that marks the site of new cartilage and vertebra (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented and shown in Figure 8.

claim: wt1b expression marks a subpopulation of sheath cells in both damage responses (needle injury and caveolin mutant-like damage).
source: We show that wt1b expression marks a subpopulation of sheath cells in both damage responses (Figure 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Homozygous wt1b mutant zebrafish show no overt difference from wild type fish in the wound response.
source: To address the function of Wt1b in the wound response, we generated a CRISPR-Cas9 genetic mutant that removes part of the C-terminal zinc-finger domains that are essential for WT1 function in mammalian systems. We find homozygous wt1b mutant zebrafish show no overt difference from wild type fish in the wound response (Figure 8; Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: A small, but significant increase in wt1a was found in wt1b∆5/∆5 wounded tissue.
source: Compensatory mechanisms have to be considered, and indeed, we find a small, but significant increase in wt1a in wt1b∆5/∆5 wounded tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: In zebrafish, ossification of the chordacentra does not require the establishment of a cartilage anlagen, but form via the direct mineralization of the fibrous notochord sheath.
source: This is completely unexpected as in zebrafish, ossification of the chordacentra does not require the establishment of a cartige anlagen, but form via the direct mineralization of the fibrous notochord sheath (Bensimon-Brito et al., 2012; Fleming et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bensimon-Brito et al., 2012 and Fleming et al., 2015.

claim: p53 is a transcription factor that in addition to its well-established role as a tumor suppressor, functions to inhibit premature osteoblast differentiation and bone remodeling.
source: p53 is a transcription factor that in addition to its well-established role as a tumor suppressor, functions to inhibit premature osteoblast differentiation and bone remodeling (Liu and Li, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liu and Li, 2010.

claim: Several lines of evidence support a direct WT1-p53 interaction, and that p53 can modify activity of WT1 transcriptional activity from an activator to a repressor on select promoters in vitro.
source: Several lines of evidence support a direct WT1-p53 interaction, and that p53 can modify activity of WT1 transcriptional activity from an activator to a repressor on select promoters in vitro (Maheswaran et al., 1995; Maheswaran et al., 1993).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Maheswaran et al., 1995 and Maheswaran et al., 1993.

claim: Loss of p53 in wt1-null mutant mice does not alter the wt1-null phenotype.
source: However, the in vivo function for the WT1-p53 interaction is not yet understood, and loss of p53 in wt1-null mutant mice does not alter the wt1-null phenotype (Menke et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Menke et al., 2002.

claim: A Wt1b-p53 axis is identified specifically in the repair of a notochord wound.
source: Here, we identify a Wt1b-p53 axis specifically in the repair of a notochord wound.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The Wt1b-p53 gene signature includes repression of genes that regulate osteogenesis in mammals, including myc (a and b), egr1 and igfrb.
source: The Wt1b-p53 gene signature includes repression of genes that regulate osteogenesis in mammals, including myc (a and b), egr1 and igfrb (Piek et al., 2010; Reumann et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Piek et al., 2010; Reumann et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2015.

claim: Repair-specific transcription factors participate in notochord healing by co-ordinating expression of cartilage genes such as sox9 and mgp, with a Wt1b-p53 transcriptional axis repressing premature expression of osteogenesis genes in the first few days following wounding.
source: We propose that repair-specific transcription factors participate in notochord healing by co-ordinating expression of cartilage genes such as sox9 and mgp (Schurgers et al., 2013; Sweatt et al., 2003; Zebboudj et al., 2002), with a Wt1b-p53 transcriptional axis repressing premature expression of osteogenesis genes in the first few days following wounding.
evidence: The claim is a proposed model based on the experimental data presented.

claim: entpd5+ notochord sheath cells are present in the wound area.
source: We see entpd5+ notochord sheath cells in the wound area (Figure 6)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: entpd5 is essential for mineralization.
source: and since entpd5 is essential for mineralization, it seems likely that these cells, in conjunction with cartilage formation at the site of injury, play a role in centrum formation (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about entpd5 function.

claim: entpd5+ cells, in conjunction with cartilage formation at the site of injury, likely play a role in centrum formation.
source: and since entpd5 is essential for mineralization, it seems likely that these cells, in conjunction with cartilage formation at the site of injury, play a role in centrum formation (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

source: Eventually, smaller vertebra form at the wound site, and wt1b:gfp cells remain tightly associated with this/these vertebra(e) into adulthood.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented.

claim: This mode of notochord wound healing and vertebra formation may be a salvage structure to effectively maintain structural integrity of the developing axial skeleton.
source: This mode of notochord wound healing and vertebra formation may be a salvage structure to effectively maintain structural integrity of the developing axial skeleton.
